prompt.adult: The LORD promised to raise up one like Moses from among their brethren. In Deuteronomy 18:18, what will He put in His mouth?
prompt.child: God promised to raise up one like Moses. What did God say He would put in that one’s mouth?
prompt.teen: Deuteronomy 18:18: “and will put” what “in His mouth”?
prompt.older: In Deuteronomy 18:18, what will the LORD put in His mouth?

verses.text: I will raise up for them a Prophet like you from among their brethren, and will put My words in His mouth, and He shall speak to them all that I command Him.

explanation.child: Look right after “and will put” in verse 18.
explanation.teen: 18:18 names the one like Moses, then what the LORD will put in His mouth. Read that phrase.

teaching.extended_explanation: 18:18 also says, “He shall speak to them all that I command Him.” 18:17 says, “What they have spoken is good.”
teaching.takeaway: The LORD will put “My words” in His mouth.

prompt.adult: Exodus 12:1 says the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron while they were in Egypt. In 12:2, what does He say this month shall be to them?
prompt.child: While they were in Egypt, the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron about the calendar. What did He say this month would be?
prompt.teen: Exodus 12:2: “This month shall be your” what?
prompt.older: Read with 12:1, what does 12:2 say this month shall be?

verses.text: Now the LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,
“This month shall be your beginning of months; it shall be the first month of the year to you.

explanation.child: Look right after “shall be your” in verse 2.
explanation.teen: 12:1 sets the speakers and the place; 12:2 names what the month shall be. Read that phrase.

teaching.extended_explanation: 12:2 also says it shall be the first month to them. 12:1 names Moses and Aaron, spoken to in Egypt.
teaching.takeaway: This month shall be your beginning of months.

prompt.adult: Leviticus 16:4 describes what Aaron shall put on his body. In 16:7, what shall he take and present before the LORD at the door of the tabernacle of meeting?
prompt.child: Before the lots were cast, Aaron had something to bring and present before the LORD. What does 16:7 say he shall take?
prompt.teen: Leviticus 16:7: “He shall take” what “and present them before the LORD”?
prompt.older: Read with 16:4, what does 16:7 say he shall take?

verses.text: He shall put the holy linen tunic and the linen trousers on his body; he shall be girded with a linen sash, and with the linen turban he shall be attired. These are holy garments. Therefore he shall wash his body in water, and put them on.
He shall take the two goats and present them before the LORD at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.

explanation.child: Look right after “He shall take” in verse 7.
explanation.teen: 16:4 names what he puts on; 16:7 names what he shall take. Read that phrase.

teaching.extended_explanation: 16:4 names what he puts on his body. 16:7 says he shall present them at the door of the tabernacle of meeting.
teaching.takeaway: He shall take the two goats.

prompt.adult: Exodus 12:6 names when they shall keep it. In 12:4, after a neighbor is included, how is the animal to be counted?
prompt.child: If one household was too small for the animal, they were to join with a neighbor. How does 12:4 say they shall count it?
prompt.teen: Exodus 12:4: “take it according to the number of” what?
prompt.older: Read with 12:6, how does 12:4 say they shall make their count?

choices.text: according to the number of the tribes
according to the number of the families
according to the number of the shepherds
according to the number of the persons

verses.text: And if the household is too small for the lamb, let him and his neighbor next to his house take it according to the number of the persons; according to each man’s need you shall make your count for the lamb.
Now you shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month. Then the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at twilight.

explanation.child: Look after “take it according to the number of” in verse 4.
explanation.teen: 12:6 names the time they keep it; 12:4 names how they count it. Read that phrase.
explanation.older: It follows “according to the number of” in 12:4.

teaching.extended_explanation: 12:4 also says, “according to each man’s need you shall make your count for the lamb.” 12:6 names the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel.
teaching.takeaway: They shall take it according to the number of the persons.

prompt.adult: Hebrews 9:6 says the priests always went into the first part of the tabernacle. In 9:1, what does the first covenant have, along with ordinances of divine service?
prompt.child: Hebrews describes what the first covenant had. Besides ordinances of divine service, what else does it name?
prompt.teen: Hebrews 9:1: “the first covenant had ordinances of divine service and” what?
prompt.older: Read with 9:6, what does 9:1 say the first covenant had, besides ordinances of divine service?

verses.text: Then indeed, even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service and the earthly sanctuary.
Now when these things had been thus prepared, the priests always went into the first part of the tabernacle, performing the services.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 1.
explanation.teen: 9:6 speaks of the priests’ service; 9:1 names two things the first covenant had. Read the second.
explanation.older: It follows “and” at the end of 9:1.

teaching.extended_explanation: 9:1 begins, “Then indeed, even the first covenant had ordinances of divine service.” 9:6 says the priests were performing the services.
teaching.takeaway: The first covenant had the earthly sanctuary.

prompt.adult: Leviticus 16:31 calls that day a sabbath of solemn rest. In 16:20, before he brings the live goat, what has he made an end of for the Holy Place, the tabernacle of meeting, and the altar?
prompt.child: After the priest finished the work for those places, he still had one animal to bring. What does the verse say he has already made an end of, for those places?
prompt.teen: Leviticus 16:20: “when he has” done what “for the Holy Place”?
prompt.older: Read with 16:31, what does 16:20 say he has made, for the Holy Place?

verses.text: “And when he has made an end of atoning for the Holy Place, the tabernacle of meeting, and the altar, he shall bring the live goat.
It is a sabbath of solemn rest for you, and you shall afflict your souls. It is a statute forever.

explanation.child: Look right after “made an end of” in verse 20.
explanation.teen: 16:31 names the kind of day; 16:20 opens with what he has made an end of. Read that word.
explanation.older: It follows “made an end of” in 16:20.

teaching.extended_explanation: 16:20 also names the Holy Place, the tabernacle of meeting, and the altar. 16:31 says, “you shall afflict your souls.”
teaching.takeaway: He has made an end of atoning for the Holy Place.

prompt.adult: Leviticus 16:32 speaks of the priest who is anointed and consecrated. In 16:14, he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the bull on the mercy seat. How does the verse say he sprinkles it?
prompt.child: Aaron sprinkled blood on the mercy seat. How does the verse say he was to sprinkle it?
prompt.teen: Leviticus 16:14: “and sprinkle it” how “on the mercy seat”?
prompt.older: Read with 16:32, how does 16:14 say he shall sprinkle the blood on the mercy seat?

verses.text: He shall take some of the blood of the bull and sprinkle it with his finger on the mercy seat on the east side; and before the mercy seat he shall sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.
And the priest, who is anointed and consecrated to minister as priest in his father’s place, shall make atonement, and put on the linen clothes, the holy garments;

explanation.child: Look right after “sprinkle it” in verse 14.
explanation.teen: 16:32 speaks of the consecrated priest; 16:14 names how he sprinkles the blood. Read that phrase.

teaching.extended_explanation: 16:32 also says he is anointed and consecrated to minister as priest in his father’s place. 16:30 says, “that you may be clean from all your sins before the LORD.”

prompt.adult: In Genesis 22:16 the LORD says, “By Myself I have sworn.” In 22:10, as they reached the place, what did Abraham stretch out his hand and take?
prompt.child: At the place of the offering, Abraham stretched out his hand. What does the verse say he took?
prompt.teen: Genesis 22:10: “and Abraham stretched out his hand and took” what?
prompt.older: Read with 22:16, what does 22:10 say Abraham took?

choices.text: took the staff to lead his son
took the fire to warm his son
took the wood to hide his son
took the knife to slay his son

verses.text: And Abraham stretched out his hand and took the knife to slay his son.
and said: “By Myself I have sworn, says the LORD, because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your son, your only son—

explanation.child: Look right after “stretched out his hand and took” in verse 10.
explanation.teen: 22:16 is the LORD’s oath; 22:10 names what Abraham took. Read that phrase.

teaching.extended_explanation: 22:16 begins, “By Myself I have sworn, says the LORD.” 22:10 says Abraham stretched out his hand.
teaching.takeaway: Abraham took the knife to slay his son.
